title: Blog Review: Sept. 16
gist: A digest of vendor engineering blogs whose single hardest data point is Siemens' Harry Foster reporting that first-silicon success among IC/ASIC respondents collapsed to 5% in 2026 from 14.4% in 2024, with the rest of the roundup (Synopsys, Cadence, Arm, Keysight, Teradyne, proteanTecs, Rambus, Quadric, Advantest, PDF Solutions) converging on the same remedy set: AI applied across the whole design flow, in-field/in-package monitoring because passing ATE no longer guarantees field success, and system-level fabrics plus 3D/PCIe connectivity for AI and HPC workloads.

insights.claim: Only 5% of IC/ASIC respondents to Siemens' latest functional verification study reported first-silicon success in 2026, down from 14.4% in 2024.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: A roughly two-thirds drop in first-pass silicon success in two years means more respins, longer tapeout-to-revenue cycles and structurally higher mask/NRE spend — bullish for verification EDA and silicon-lifecycle tooling vendors, bearish for fabless margin and schedule guidance.
insights.quote: first-silicon success has fallen sharply, with only 5% of IC/ASIC respondents to the latest functional verification study reporting first-silicon success in 2026, compared with 14.4% in 2024
insights.locator: Siemens' Harry Foster finds that first-silicon

insights.claim: Design complexity has outrun existing verification methodology to the point that respins are now the overwhelming norm rather than the exception, which is the implicit justification for the AI-in-verification push the rest of the EDA industry is selling.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: Watch EDA vendors monetize the respin problem: verification and AI-flow attach rates are the leading indicator for EDA revenue growth outpacing wafer starts.
insights.locator: Siemens' Harry Foster finds that first-silicon

insights.claim: Synopsys argues chip development is hitting an engineering capacity crunch in which implementing AI across the entire design flow — not in isolated point tools — is necessary just to sustain the current pace of innovation.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: Frames AI-EDA as a headcount substitute rather than a productivity nice-to-have, which supports premium pricing and full-flow lock-in for Synopsys and Cadence against point-tool competitors.
insights.quote: as chip development faces an engineering capacity crunch, implementing AI across the entire flow becomes necessary to sustain the pace of innovation

insights.claim: Cadence is pushing a shift from established SoC design paradigms to system-level fabrics purpose-built for next-generation AI, HPC and data center workloads.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: Interconnect/fabric IP is becoming the differentiator in AI silicon; watch IP licensing revenue mix shift toward fabric and NoC vendors as monolithic SoC designs give way to fabric-connected systems.
insights.quote: transforming established SoC design paradigms into system-level fabrics capable of supporting next-gen AI, HPC, and data center workloads

insights.claim: Timing closure at advanced nodes now requires explicitly modeling on-chip variation and common path pessimism removal when computing the minimum clock period, because nominal timing no longer predicts real-world reliability.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: Variation-driven timing margin is where achievable clock frequency is silently lost — a direct link between process variation control and the performance a chip can actually ship at.
insights.locator: Cadence's P. Saisrinivas introduces how to calculate

insights.claim: Arm is promoting ExecuTorch as the means to partition and optimize a single PyTorch model across CPUs, GPUs and NPUs using five target-specific execution paths.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: Whoever owns the partitioning runtime owns the edge AI software moat; Arm extending from CPU ISA into cross-accelerator model deployment is a defensive move against NPU vendors capturing the toolchain.
insights.quote: use ExecuTorch to partition and optimize one PyTorch model across CPUs, GPUs, and NPUs using five target-specific execution paths
insights.locator: Arm's Ash Naik shows how to use ExecuTorch

insights.claim: Arm reports combining a novel weight format with quantization-aware training to shrink multimodal AI model size while retaining accuracy.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: Model compression that preserves multimodal accuracy is the gating factor for on-device AI; every step here reduces the addressable market for cloud inference on the lightest workloads.
insights.locator: Arm's Jeevan Bhoot demonstrates a method

insights.claim: Quadric argues for a single software-controlled core that executes matrix, vector and scalar code in one pipeline, implicitly a bet against the prevailing multi-block CPU-plus-NPU-plus-GPU heterogeneous edge architecture.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: Directly contradicts the Arm heterogeneous-partitioning pitch in the same digest — a live architectural fork in edge AI silicon worth tracking for which design wins accumulate.
insights.quote: a single, software-controlled core that handles matrix, vector, and scalar code in one execution pipeline
insights.locator: Quadric's Steve Roddy digs into the advantages

insights.claim: Teradyne states that passing automated test equipment no longer guarantees a device will succeed in the field, breaking the long-standing assumption that final test is the quality gate.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: If ATE pass is no longer sufficient, spend migrates from one-time test to continuous in-field monitoring and silicon lifecycle management — a structural share shift among test and analytics vendors.
insights.quote: why passing ATE no longer guarantees success in the field

insights.claim: proteanTecs argues every individual chiplet inside a system-in-package must be monitored, not just the package as a whole.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: Per-chiplet monitoring IP attaches per die rather than per package, so its unit economics scale with chiplet count — a leveraged play on advanced packaging adoption.
insights.locator: proteanTecs' Nir Sever explains why it's critical

insights.claim: Synopsys is pushing alignment of production measurements with actual device behavior and pre-silicon expectations, implying today's production data and design models are materially disconnected.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: Closing the pre-silicon-to-production data loop is the same problem set as the first-silicon success collapse; it is where EDA vendors are building recurring-revenue analytics businesses.
insights.locator: Synopsys' Guy Cortez, Dan Alexandrescu, and Aaron Barker explain

insights.claim: PDF Solutions highlights a disparity between how much data chip manufacturing generates and how little of it actually gets analyzed.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: Unanalyzed fab data is the stated whitespace for manufacturing analytics vendors; the gap is the TAM argument for PDF Solutions and peers.
insights.quote: the disparity between how much data is generated during chip manufacturing and what gets analyzed
insights.locator: PDF Solutions' Christophe Begue looks at

insights.claim: Nordson identifies bond testing as an emerging critical control point for long-term performance and yield.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: As value migrates into stacked and bonded packages, bond integrity metrology becomes a new mandatory step — watch for tool spend shifting toward packaging-stage inspection.
insights.locator: Nordson's YiPeng Zhou finds that bond testing

insights.claim: Onto Innovation is targeting better visibility into deposition variation as a process control lever.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: Deposition variation control ties directly to the on-chip variation that limits achievable clock frequency — metrology spend is an upstream proxy for advanced-node performance yield.
insights.locator: Onto Innovation's Huayuan Li, Alex Hong

insights.claim: Rambus is building configurable PCIe subsystems designed to span local expansion, shared resource domains and longer-reach topologies from a single IP base.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: Configurable PCIe spanning disaggregated and pooled-resource topologies is the IP layer under rack-scale disaggregation — a direct read on data center architecture shifting away from fixed server boundaries.
insights.quote: building configurable PCIe subsystems that span local expansion, shared resource domains, and longer-reach topologies

insights.claim: Synopsys is implementing 64.0 GT/s PCIe connectivity inside a stacked-die, face-to-face 3D architecture.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: PCIe 6-class signaling routed through face-to-face 3D stacks is a concrete marker that high-speed SerDes IP is moving into the 3D-IC domain, raising the packaging and IP content per AI device.
insights.quote: the implementation of 64.0 GT/s PCIe connectivity in a stacked-die, face-to-face 3D architecture

themes.theme: AI security and supply chain trust

insights.claim: Keysight warns that AI systems introduce entirely new classes of security risk to enterprise environments, requiring a dedicated comprehensive AI security assessment framework rather than extensions of existing IT security practice.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: A new security category rather than a feature line means a fresh budget line and new vendor entrants — watch AI-specific assessment and red-teaming offerings from test and measurement incumbents.
insights.quote: AI systems introduce entirely new classes of security risks to enterprise environments, driving the need for a comprehensive AI security assessment framework

insights.claim: SEMI is framing counterfeit electronics, traceability and trusted hardware as problems solvable only through industry collaboration across the semiconductor ecosystem rather than by individual firms.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: Collective traceability standards create compliance-driven demand for provenance tooling; the AI-infrastructure framing means counterfeit risk is now a data center procurement issue, not just a defense/aerospace one.
insights.locator: SEMI's Mayura Padmanabhan and Nishita Rao chat

insights.claim: Advantest and ISIG are focusing on supply chain interdependencies and strategic alliances as a determinant of semiconductor outcomes, treating partnership structure rather than technology alone as the competitive variable.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: Alliance formation among test, materials and packaging suppliers is a leading signal of where consolidation and preferred-supplier lock-in will occur.
insights.locator: Advantest's Don Ong sits down with ISIG's Salah Nasri
